verdict.rationale: Phaser's own docs show 2D as its native workflow: sprites are created with this.add.sprite, sprite sheets and atlases are first-class loader assets, frame-based animation is the primary animation model, and Arcade Physics gives sprites 2D velocity, acceleration and gravity (limited to rectangles and circles). Community users confirm it is a 2D-focused framework. Tilemaps, however, are evidenced only by a 'tilemap & atlas editors' line in the paid editor's pricing and one community mention, with no first-party engine docs for tilemap loading or rendering. Missing for 10: first-party engine documentation of runtime tilemap support (loading, layers, tile collision); docs for 2D physics beyond the limited Arcade system (e.g. polygon/complex shapes); hands-on corroboration of tilemap workflows.

support.subject: As a game developer, 2D is a first-class workflow — sprites, tilemaps, 2D physics — not a 3D afterthought

citations.quote: This will allow you to control the Sprite using the built-in physics functions, such as velocity, acceleration, gravity, etc.
It's a lightweight physics system that can only handle two different types of physics shapes: rectangles and circles.
It's a great tool if you go for a game that fits this framework - 2D, sprites, tilemaps, physics
